author: TEDx Talks
description:
As artificial intelligence becomes a bigger part of our lives, how can we stay not just useful but truly valuable? Duncan Wardle, former Head of Innovation & Creativity at Disney, believes the answer lies in something simple and powerful: being human.

In this engaging and thought-provoking talk, Duncan invites us to reconnect with the skills we were all born with but often leave behind as we grow up. Creativity. Intuition. Empathy. Curiosity. Imagination. Through real stories and practical examples, he shows how these human traits can help us solve problems, spark new ideas, and create experiences that no machine ever could. Duncan Wardle began his remarkable 30 year career at the Walt Disney Company in 1986 as a barman in the Rose & Crown Pub at Epcot. He rose to  become Head of Innovation & Creativity, where Duncan helped teams at Disney Parks, Lucasfilm, Marvel, Pixar, Imagineering and Animation to innovate, creating magical new storylines and amazing experiences for consumers aro
title: A Disney Imagineer's lessons on creativity | Duncan Wardle | TEDxDurham

author: TEDx Talks
description: Carlie Schofield shares a deeply personal account of intergenerational trauma, revealing how silence and history can shape lives across generations. It’s a call to see trauma as something we can work with rather than something that defines us.  Carlie Schofield has worked as a counsellor and cultural consultant for the past 12 years. As an Aboriginal woman and mother, Carlie’s work explores how intergenerational trauma, perfectionism, and silence shape women’s emotional lives and how reclaiming safety and self-leadership can change entire family legacies. She works as a Cultural Advisor and Indigenous Mental Health Professional at MindSpot and is an Associate Lecturer in Indigenous Trauma Recovery at the University of Wollongong. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The inheritance no one talks about | Carlie Schofield | TEDxWollongong

description: Monica’s TEDx program will trace her personal and professional journey from childhood ambitions to executive leadership in conservation. Monica’s career path has been anything but predictable, starting with early dreams of becoming a TV anchor and evolving in ways she never could have imagined. She will share not only the tough lessons learned along the way but the joy of taking a “yes, and” approach to career development and personal growth that has led to one of her greatest experiences yet – leading one of the largest, most impactful environmental organizations in Georgia. Monica is a seventh generation Georgian who has dedicated her career to uplifting the people and places. As Executive Director for The Nature Conservancy, Georgia, Monica leads ambitious land and water protection initiatives by building partnerships. Her impact on this state includes securing over $100 million for public health and environmental causes and fostering sustainable partnerships that drive meaningful,
title: Embracing fear, failure, and embarrassment – The fast track to success | Monica Thornton | TEDxEmory

author: TEDx Talks
description: "Fail First: A Two-Step Guide to Becoming a Resilient Researcher" Explores how embracing failure in research can build resilience and lead to greater scientific growth and discovery. Lama Alshamroukh is a biology pre-med student at West Virginia University and a driven student leader passionate about research, mentorship, and academic excellence. She serves as an Eberly College Student Ambassador and a Presidential Student Ambassador, and she is actively involved in multiple research environments that reflect her long-term goal of pursuing medicine. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Fail First: A Two-Step Guide to Becoming a Resilient Researcher | Lama Alshamroukh | TEDxWVU

author: TEDx Talks
description: "Am I Good Enough to Have Imposter Syndrome? How Vulnerability is an Asset" Challenges the idea that success silences self-doubt, arguing that leaning into vulnerability is key to reaching your fullest potential. Dr. Lauren Bojarski is a neurologist, assistant Professor, and associate program director at at the WVU Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute who is redefining the "art of resilience" through the lens of vulnerability. Despite a decorated career—including a "Rising Star" award, a "Kentucky Colonel" commission, and the national ACGME David C. Leach Award for her contributions to resident education—Dr. Bojarski once found herself paralyzed by a panic attack in the ER, convinced she was a fraud. This pivotal moment revealed a profound truth: professional excellence does not cure "imposter phenomenon"—the persistent feeling of being a fraud despite clear evidence of success. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local co
title: Am I Good Enough to Have Imposter Syndrome? | Lauren Bojarski | TEDxWVU

description: How knowing and living your purpose can keep you grounded through loss, burnout, and change. In this steady and deeply human talk, this idea explores why purpose is not something we chase when life is working, but something we lean on when it is not. What it offers is something solid to hold onto when everything else feels uncertain. Through personal storytelling, research, and real-world leadership experience, the talk reframes purpose as practical and human. Through stories of loss, recovery, leadership, and empathy in action, the talk shows how purpose becomes an anchor that helps us stay steady when life feels overwhelming. title: How to Make Purpose Your Lifeline When Life Gets Hard | Melissa Fors Shackelford | TEDxDuluth

author: TEDx Talks
description: "Let Your Ambition Fly: From Concept to Confirmation" Uses her journey across disciplines and continents to show how bold ambition paired with purposeful action can bring ideas to life. Zim Warda Hasan is a PhD student in the Clinical and Translational Science (CTS) program at West Virginia University. She currently works as a graduate research assistant with the WVU Medicine Gastroenterology and Hepatology team. Originally from Chittagong, Bangladesh, Zim earned her medical degree in her home country and later completed her master’s degree at Western Kentucky University. Her recent work focuses on addressing the “treatment gap” in obesity care by supporting clinical studies that explore options between lifestyle change, medication, and less invasive procedures. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Let Your Ambition Fly: From Concept to Confirmation | Zim Hasan | TEDxWVU

author: TEDx Talks
description: We need the law to deliver justice, but what happens when it messes up? This talk shares the story of a woman falsely accused of killing her own child. Built on flawed evidence and systemic biases, the case resulted in an infamous miscarriage of justice and destroyed numerous lives forever. Yet, this tragedy shines a light on grave failures in the legal system - and reveal why real change actually starts with asking better questions. Bhadra Panicker is a Law and Business student at Trinity College Dublin. As a Laidlaw Scholar, she conducted research on miscarriages of justice against women, developing her passion for feminist jurisprudence. Her work combines academic work with practical engagement to platform conversations about achieving equality and empowerment in the law. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: When the Law Gets It Wrong | Bhadra Panicker | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: We’ve spent a century mastering technology. The next century will test whether we can master ourselves. As AI, automation, and immersive realities reshape how we work, learn, and lead, the real challenge isn’t keeping up with machines: it’s staying human in the process. This talk explores what truly drives change when technology evolves faster than people do. Drawing on insights from my work at the Trinity AI-XR Innovation Lab and European projects on responsible AI, I’ll unpack how human curiosity, empathy, and adaptability, not algorithms, remain the most powerful engines of transformation. This is not a talk about technology. It’s a call to reimagine education, leadership, and society for a world where change is constant, and humanity is our competitive advantage. If the last 100 years were about building intelligent systems, the next 100 will be about further developing human skills. Progress isn’t about replacing people, it’s about redesigning the future together through human-te
title: The human equation in an age of intelligent machines | Na Fu | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Blockchain and digital assets are moving from the margins to the core of the global financial system. What began as an experiment in digital money is now reshaping how value is stored, transferred, and governed. The question is no longer whether this transformation will happen, but which countries will help shape it. Ireland is uniquely positioned for this moment. We combine deep financial services expertise, a strong technology ecosystem, access to the European market, and a reputation for credible, forward-looking regulation. These strengths already exist — but too often in isolation. This talk explores how Ireland can “bring the pieces together” by aligning policy, education, industry, and innovation. The goal is not hype, but responsible leadership: building trusted digital asset infrastructure, attracting high-quality firms, and helping define the standards of the next era of finance. Blockchain isn’t just a technology trend. It’s a shift in how trust works in a digital world — a
title: The Ecosystem to Maximise the Blockchain Opportunity  | Lory Kehoe | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Linda Djougang moved from Cameroon to Ireland at the age of nine, full of dreams but unsure where she belonged. After secondary school, she lacked the points for any course. In that moment, she felt lost, unseen and uncertain of who she was meant to become. What she didn’t realise then was that failure was not the end, it was the beginning of a different kind of journey.  At eighteen, she was accept to the Trinity Access Programme. At nineteen, she discovered rugby. She had never played a sport before, yet it became her teacher, community, and mirror. Through it, she learned discipline, courage, and how to be her own leader. Balancing nursing studies, training, and self-doubt, she discovered that resilience isn’t about never falling, it’s about finding the strength to rise every time you do. From taking three buses a day to training to eventually wearing the Irish green jersey, she learned that failure can be a foundation, and that true leadership is not about power but presence, not
title: A different journey: From rejection to resilience | Linda Djougang | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Hunting for transiting exomoons around a brown dwarf: What if the absence of something could change how we understand the universe? Brown dwarfs are these mysterious objects that are intermediate objects between planets and stars, too massive to be planets, yet too small to shine like stars. One such object, 2MASS J10475385+2124234, challenges what we think we know. Despite drifting alone through space without a solar system, it produces powerful aurorae, like the beautiful glowing light seen on Earth. On planets like Jupiter, aurorae are powered by its orbiting moon Io. But what happens when there may be no moon at all? This talk explores how data from the James Webb Space Telescope was used to search for an exomoon by tracking subtle changes in brightness as the brown dwarf rotates and flickers. The results reveal no clear evidence of a moon, pointing instead to dynamic weather and magnetic activity within the brown dwarf itself. This talk highlights the potential of JWST to probe i
title: Cloudy with a Chance of Exomoons | Ishna Tripathi | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if a friend’s success didn’t diminish one’s own chances, but increased them? When opportunities feel scarce, a friend’s or colleague’s success can feel like a loss, and jealousy can follow. But this reaction to others’ achievements assumes success is isolated, rather than multiplying through social networks, expanding access for those nearby. Drawing on the sociological concept of homophily—the tendency for people to form close relationships with others who share similar values and traits—this talk reframes success from a zero-sum to an abundance mindset. Because social networks are comprised of like-minded people, one person’s success often creates opportunities that naturally fit the others. When someone within a close network enters a new relationship, career path, or community, they don’t just change their own circumstances, they expand the network itself. Seen through this lens, jealousy is transformed from a fear of lost opportunity into an understanding of how others’ succ
title: Rethinking jealousy—how others’ success becomes your own | Evie Kramer | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: As a neuroscientist turned creative psychotherapist specialising in play therapy, my story sits at the intersection of science, humanity, and unexpected change. During my PhD, I was fascinated by how relationships and experience shape the developing brain. But while writing my final chapters, life shifted course: I became a mother to a newborn with Down syndrome. That moment didn’t end my path — it transformed it. Motherhood reshaped my understanding of growth, healing, and what it means to truly attune to another person. It led me from the lab into the therapy room, where I discovered that the neuroplasticity I once studied in theory comes alive in the spontaneous, creative language of children at play. This talk explores how our training never leaves us; it evolves with us. The scientific lens I once used to study neurons now guides how I understand safety, connection, and resilience in my clinical work. And the unexpected journey I hadn’t planned for revealed gifts I couldn’t have
title: My journey into play | Wen Wan Wang-Whelan | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the future of business leadership was guided by Indigenous wisdom? Across cultures, Indigenous knowledge systems emphasise reciprocity, community, and stewardship of Mother Earth — principles modern economies urgently need to relearn. This talk explores what it would mean to instil an Indigenous Mindset into the education of future business leaders and why this idea holds practical lessons for individuals and organisations worldwide.  Drawing from longitudinal research with Lakota elders, leaders and tribal communities in East Africa and India’s Sundarban Islands, I contrast Western and Indigenous worldviews of value, leadership, and sustainable market creation. By bridging these perspectives we can reimagine business as a force for regeneration.  This talk challenges us to expand the boundaries of how and where knowledge resides. Individuals can adopt principles of balance, and organisations can embed Indigenous-informed strategies. Audiences can rediscover what Indigenous tr
title: Remembering the future - Why past wisdom matters now | Ronika Chakrabarti | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description: I research and teach cross-cultural management, a field built to help us develop cultural understanding to improve how we work, lead, and connect across cultures. Yet those conversations are becoming harder to have. The very dialogue my discipline depends on is the one people are increasingly afraid to enter. Recently, I asked a group of executives, “What does it mean to be from your culture?” Silence. Eventually, one said, “I’d rather not answer…I might offend someone. What it means for me may not be the same for someone else.” That moment stopped me. In our well-intentioned pursuit of inclusivity, cultural curiosity is being replaced by cultural caution. We are so afraid of saying the wrong thing that we say nothing at all. And when fear silences conversation, learning disappears. We begin to confuse politeness with progress. title: The chilling effect of cultural silence  | Eimear Nolan | TEDxTrinityCollegeDublin
